newsitem.title: UKRAINE: UKRAINE GOVT SEEKS CASH FOR SUGAR BEET BUYING PLAN.
newsitem.headline: UKRAINE GOVT SEEKS CASH FOR SUGAR BEET BUYING PLAN.

text.p: Ukraine's government is still trying to figure out how to raise money for a sugar-beet buying scheme it implemented this year in an effort to save its sugar market, Agriculture Minister Yuri Karasyk said on Thursday.
"The banks are working on it," Karasyk told his first news conference since being appointed late last month.
The plan, announced by former minister Mykhailo Zubets, was to pay producers 70 hryvnias ($37.75) per tonne of sugar beets in a bid to inject cash into the market and stop widespread bartering.
But the cash-strapped government has yet to announce where the money would come from to pay growers.
Critics of the scheme said the government would never pay producers and take the beets for itself.

The plan also called for sowing less sugar beet to reduce oversupply, limiting domestic sugar sales to 1.5 million tonnes at a government-set minimum price of 1.19 hryvnias, and selling leftover sugar abroad at world prices.
